problem.title: Why You Need a Partner
problem.description: Physical AI is evolving fast. But who decides today on the right entry point without hands-on experience? That's exactly the gap we fill.

evaluation.title: No Evaluation Framework
evaluation.description: Which robot can do what? Without real-world experience, decisions are a shot in the dark.

access.title: Technology Feels Out of Reach
access.description: AI and robotics seem like topics only for large corporations -- not for mid-sized companies.

trust.title: No Independent Knowledge
trust.description: Manufacturers sell their own solutions. Independent, hands-on data and neutral advice are missing.

dependency.title: Dependency as a Security Risk
dependency.description: Many robots send camera and sensor data to clouds outside Europe and receive updates nobody reviews. Whoever controls the models and data controls the robot.

sovereignty.title: Your robots. Your data.
sovereignty.intro: A cognitive robot is a networked computer with cameras, microphones, and actuators -- right on your shop floor, next to your people. Whoever controls its models, data, and updates controls the robot. That is why we design Physical AI for sovereignty and security from day one.

diagram.aria: Diagram: data and models stay within three protection zones -- on the robot, in your plant, and in Europe. Uncontrolled outbound data flow is blocked.

data.label: Data
data.title: Data Sovereignty
data.description: Camera, sensor, and process data stay in your plant or in European data centers. GDPR-compliant, no outflow to third countries -- you decide what gets shared.

models.label: Models
models.title: Open Models
models.description: Open-weight models you can inspect, adapt, and run yourself. No black box whose behavior changes overnight through a cloud update.

compute.label: Operations
compute.title: Edge & On-Premise
compute.description: Inference on the robot or on your own hardware inside your network. Critical operations do not depend on an internet connection or on a vendor’s pricing policy.

security.label: Cybersecurity
security.title: Security by Design
security.description: Network segmentation, signed updates, access and permission concepts, audit logging. We assess robots like any other device on your OT network -- before they enter the shop floor.

safety.label: Safety
safety.title: Protecting People
safety.description: Human-robot collaboration needs clear safety concepts: risk assessment, speed and force limits, emergency stop, and fallback strategies for when the AI gets it wrong.

compliance.label: Regulation
compliance.title: EU Rules in View
compliance.description: EU AI Act, Machinery Regulation, Cyber Resilience Act, and NIS2: we translate the requirements into concrete technical checkpoints for your project.

checklist.title: Five questions before a robot joins your network
items: Where are camera and sensor data processed and stored?
Does the robot keep working without a cloud connection?
Who can install updates -- and can you review them first?
Can you switch the AI model or run it yourself?
How are people in the work area protected when the AI is wrong?
checklist.note: If an answer stays vague, that is a finding. We help you put it in context.

loop.caption: Learning loop: every deployment becomes shared knowledge.
loop.aria: Animated learning loop: deployment produces data, data becomes knowledge that improves the next deployment.

openSource.title: Open-Source AI

embodiedAi.a: Embodied AI (EmAI) means: artificial intelligence that operates in a physical body -- cognitive robots. Unlike pure software AI, these systems interact directly with the physical world. We help companies understand this technology and use it meaningfully.

cognitiveRobots.a: Cognitive robots are robots that can learn through AI models, adapt, and work in unstructured environments. They can grasp, carry, assemble, and collaborate with humans -- and are becoming more capable through open AI models.

workshops.a: Our workshops are hands-on: participants experience cognitive robots in action, understand how AI models are trained, and assess whether automation makes sense for their company. We offer on-site and virtual formats.

dataCollection.a: We collect performance data from real deployments: success rates, error types, energy consumption, cycle times, and practical limits. This data is vendor-independent and helps companies make informed decisions.

openSource.a: Open AI models provide transparency, independence, and community-driven innovation. No vendor lock-in, no proprietary black boxes. Companies keep control over their technology decisions.

sovereignty.q: What does sovereign Physical AI mean?
sovereignty.a: Sovereign Physical AI means you stay in control of your robots’ data, models, and updates. Data stays in your plant or in Europe, models are open and replaceable, and operations do not depend on a single vendor or on a cloud outside Europe. That keeps you able to act -- technically, legally, and economically.

security.a: That depends on the architecture -- which is exactly what we assess. We look at two levels: cybersecurity (network segmentation, access control, signed updates, audit logging) and functional safety for people in the work area (risk assessment, force and speed limits, emergency stop, fallback strategies). Both belong in the evaluation before a robot goes into production.

humanAssist.a: No -- cognitive robots fill gaps created by labor shortages. They take over repetitive, physically demanding, or dangerous tasks and enable employees to focus on more qualified, value-adding work. People remain at the center.

consulting.a: We analyze your processes, evaluate automation needs, and create a realistic roadmap. What's possible today? What's coming in 1-2 years? How do you prepare your company? Independent and vendor-neutral.
